newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian money market inactive as RBI closed.
newsitem.headline: Indian money market inactive as RBI closed.

text.p: The Indian money market was inactive on Monday as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was closed for public business on account of its half-yearly closing of accounts, dealers said.
Call money was not traded but traders were looking to trade in government securities for next day value, they said.
"Call money is not being traded today," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "But there are a few quotes for governemnt securiites. There may be a few trades later in the day for tomorrow value."
He said the prices being quoted were at weekend levels.
"We will have to wait and see what happens tomorrow," he said. "As call money eased on Saturday, we can expect some demand for securities and prices may go up."
Call money eased on Saturday to 4.25-4.75 percent from the previous close of 8.75-9.0 percent on funds inflows from an RBI repurchase of government securities.
